title: May the rule tests of ST-STD-CODE hold STEGO's own tree to a list of known faults that can only get shorter?
description: The tests ST-STD-CODE-R01-T01 to R06-T01 expect no fault in STEGO's own tree. On 2026-10-31 the tree has 407 faults: 5 packages that two domains name (R01), 23 records whose title is not declared in their file (R02), 18 imports against the domain order (R03), 225 test files that name no test record (R04), 136 source files that no record names (R05), and no stub (R06). A test that expects no fault fails at each commit until all are fixed, so no proof run can pass. The tests now read a committed list of known faults, the tooling record ST-ASR-TOOL03: a fault that is not on the list fails the test, and a listed fault that is gone fails it too, so the list can only get shorter. Options: accept the list until it is empty, and change the then of each rule test to say so; keep the rule tests not automated until the tree has no fault; or keep the list for the change gate and add one test per rule that expects no fault for the release gate.

title: Which technical record names assure.CodeFaults, the one function the gates call for the code-standard faults?
description: CodeFaults in internal/assure/code_standard.go runs the six predicates ST-ASR-SP05-PR to ST-ASR-SP10-PR over the tree and the spec at a commit and returns their faults in order. The gate handlers ST-ASR-CMD02-H and ST-ASR-CMD03-H will call it for ST-ASR-UC02-R05 and ST-ASR-UC03-R04. No record names it: a predicate record has no description in which to name it, and no domain service exists for it, so a service record is wrong. Options: add a domain service, such as Find the code faults, with its service record assure.CodeFaults; let the descriptions of the gate handlers name it; or accept that a function which only joins the predicates of records needs no record of its own.
